text: A long bench under the window, and on it a rope-walk in miniature:
hemp, wax, and three strands going into one.
Every haulage rope in the workings came off a bench like this one.
The kitchen, squeezed into what the workshop left of the room.
The workshop got the window. The cooking got the corner.
Coils of finished rope stacked to the ceiling, sized by fathom.
None of them have been sold. The Hall buys one a year now
and the Hall is the only customer left.
A framed certificate: STONEWAKE ROPEWORKS, EST. 71 YEARS.
Underneath it, unframed, a letter from the Foundation offering to buy
the whole of the ropewalk, the premises, and the name.
